applied.problem: "Three times one line's healthy current" is stated of every first fault but holds for a solid fault (a fault with resistance passes less); "charge and discharge 60 times a second" is said of all AC; doubling the cable doubles C only if cable is all of it; 3 × 96 is 288, so 287 is "about".

The worked example writes 3 × 192 = 575, but 3 × 192 is 576 (575 comes from the unrounded 191.5 mA); "multiply by 3" gives a solid fault's current, and a fault through some resistance passes less. Other figures checked: 0.29 A per µF, 1 µF + 1 µF = 2 µF, 192 mA, 10 µF at 277 V gives about 1.04 A.

"The plot is a straight line through zero in Fault on L1" fails with the drives on, which add a fixed 1 µF so the line is offset. All screen figures recomputed and correct (2,650 Ω, 96/166/287 mA, 575 mA, 1.44 A, 830 mA, 190 and 36 mA body currents, 0.35/0.60/1.04 A, 800 Ω per Eaton).
"The three healthy currents cancel" is exact only for perfectly equal capacitance; a real system is a little unbalanced, as screen 4 says, so a little is left over.
